newsitem.title: USA: GM supplier Delco Remy reaches tentative labor pact.
newsitem.headline: GM supplier Delco Remy reaches tentative labor pact.

text.p: Bargainers for the United Auto Workers union and auto supplier Delco Remy America Inc reached a tentative contract early Saturday, averting a strike that would have deprived General Motors Corp. of starter motors for nearly all of its North American-built vehicles.
Union leaders and company officials would not disclose terms of the tentative contract, which covers about 1,500 workers in Anderson, Indiana and Meridian, Mississippi.

But UAW President Stephen Yokich and other leaders released a statement indicating the bargaining had gone well. The UAW was demanding that Anderson-based Delco Remy match the pattern agreed to by the Big Three automakers last November, and hire about 440 temporary workers on a permanent basis.
"UAW-represented workers at Delco Remy America should be pleased with this fine, new agreement," the UAW said in the statement.

The pact was reached about at 4 a.m. EST Saturday, four hours after a midnight Friday strike deadline expired. Delco Remy spokesman John Pyzik said talks continued past the deadline without a walkout. He said scheduled Saturday overtime at the company's plants would continue as planned.
About 1,100 workers in Anderson belong to UAW Local 662. Another 400 work in Meridian and belong to Local 2185. Ratification meetings are set for next week, the union said.

The contract is the first time Delco Remy has negotiated with the UAW since it was sold by GM to a management group led by former Chrysler Corp. executive Harold Sperlich in 1994. The company had agreed to abide by the terms of the 1993-96 agreement until a new pact was reached.

The Delco Remy talks marked the second time a supplier spun off from GM nearly faced a strike over contract talks. Last month, American Axle & Manufacturing Inc. reached a new contract minutes before a strike deadline set by the UAW.

In those talks, American Axle agreed to follow the Big Three pattern, which calls for lump-sum payments of $2,000 in the first year and 3 percent raises in the second and third years. The contracts also include a guarantee to maintain employment at 95 percent of the current work force level over the life of the agreement and generous improvments in pension benefits.

Elsewhere in Indiana Saturday, GM was scheduled to resume bargaining aimed at resolving a UAW strike at a truck plant that reached its ninth day Saturday. About 2,700 members of UAW Local 2209 walked off the job at GM's Fort Wayne full-size pickup truck plant March 14 after the two sides failed to agree on terms for a new local contract.
UAW leaders are demanding GM address health and safety grievances and add more workers to reduce overtime.
